intent: "Read me the thread before I answer" — every message in order, who is on it, what we have decided it means, and what it is attached to

input_schema.title: conversation.get input
input_schema.description: One page of one thread's messages. The thread names itself: a read on request names no campaign, and a work item's campaign is carried for context only.

external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the thread, as `conversation.list` returned it.

limit.description: At most this many messages on the page. Required: absence is not a default, and a page may come back shorter.

offset.description: Where the page starts in the provider's own order: 0 for the first page, then the previous page's `offset` plus the number of items it returned.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

subject.description: The subject the thread's messages carry, or null where the channel has none.

contact.description: The person on the thread as the provider names them, or null when it names nobody.

has_ai_draft.description: Whether the provider holds a drafted answer. The draft itself is never returned.

external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the message, or null when it gives none.

direction.description: `inbound` the other side wrote it, `outbound` this account did, `unknown` when the provider does not say.

sent_at.description: When it was sent, in UTC.

from.description: Who wrote it: an address, or a display name where the channel has no address.

to.description: The recipients as the provider lists them, at most ten; null when it lists none.

cc.description: The copied recipients as the provider lists them, at most ten; null when it lists none.

bcc.description: The blind-copied recipients as the provider lists them, at most ten; null when it lists none.

body.description: The message as the provider holds it, markup included, at most 12000 characters; null when it holds none.

truncated.description: Whether `body` was cut at its 12000 characters.

has_more.description: Whether the thread holds more messages after this page.

ordering.description: The order `offset` counts in: the first message first.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no thread under this identifier, or not one this account may see.
The provider account's plan or role does not include this capability, so no call by this account can answer it.
The provider's answer was larger than this installation lets a plugin read from a program (`Plugins:Exec:OutputBytes`), so it was cut off; asking again would cut it the same way.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read conversations for this account.
The provider refused the read for now and it may be asked again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing and costs nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: Messages come oldest first, which `vendor.ordering` states.
A page holds at most `limit` messages, starting at `offset` in the provider's own order, and `has_more` says whether more follow.

A page may come back short of `limit` with `has_more: true`: the plugin stops before the result would pass 768 KiB, counted as the runtime counts it (six bytes for DEL, for every character outside ASCII and for each of `<`, `>`, `&`, `'`, `"`, `+` and the backtick, twelve for one outside the Basic Multilingual Plane).
The next page starts at `offset` plus the number of items this page returned, never at `offset + limit`.
A body longer than 12000 characters is cut where a character ends, and that message says `truncated: true`.
A thread whose whole history is more than the plugin may read from the provider in one answer fails `provider_answer_too_large`, permanently: asking again would cut it the same way.
A thread the provider does not hold, or one this account may not see, fails `conversation_not_found` as permanent.
A drafted answer the provider holds is reported as `vendor.has_ai_draft` and never returned.
